description: React components that execute exclusively on the server. Default component type in Next.js App Router. Output is serialized as RSC Payload and never includes component source code or secrets in the client bundle.
constraints: Cannot use React client hooks: useState, useEffect, useReducer, useContext, etc.
Cannot use browser-only APIs: window, document, localStorage, navigator, etc.
Cannot attach event handlers: onClick, onChange, onSubmit, etc.
Cannot use React context as a consumer — context is not supported in Server Components
Props passed to Client Components must be serializable by React
Cannot import client-only modules without wrapping in a Client Component boundary
Cannot be made interactive without delegating to a Client Component
Async Server Components must be awaited at the point of composition
Environment variables without NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix are safe to use and will NOT leak to client
allowedPatterns: Async/await data fetching directly in component body
Direct database access via ORM or database client — credentials excluded from client bundle
Access to server-side secrets, API keys, tokens via environment variables
Passing serializable data as props to Client Components
Passing Server Components as children or props to Client Components
Using React.cache() to deduplicate requests across the component tree
Sequential or parallel async data fetching with Promise.all / Promise.allSettled
Importing the server-only package to enforce server-only module boundaries
Using fetch() with next.tags, next.revalidate, or cache options
Using use cache directive to cache computation results
forbiddenPatterns: createContext() consumption inside a Server Component
onClick, onChange, or any event handler attached directly in JSX
window, document, localStorage, sessionStorage, navigator access
Importing client-only packages (e.g. packages using window) without a Client Component wrapper
Passing non-serializable values (functions, class instances, Promises without use()) as props to Client Components
Marking an entire layout or root component as 'use client' unnecessarily
runtimeBehavior: Executes only on the server — never sent to or re-executed on the client
Rendered into RSC Payload: a compact binary representation of the rendered component tree
RSC Payload contains: rendered output of Server Components, placeholders for Client Components with JS file references, serialized props passed to Client Components
On first load: HTML is generated from Server Components for immediate non-interactive preview
On subsequent navigations: RSC Payload is fetched and used to reconcile the component tree — no HTML re-generation
Identical fetch() calls within the same render are automatically memoized — safe to call in multiple components without deduplication logic
fetch() requests are not cached by default — each request fetches fresh data unless cache: 'force-cache' or use cache is used
Routes with uncached fetch requests are rendered dynamically at request time
Routes with only cached or static data are prerendered at build time (static rendering)
Rendering is split into chunks by route segment — each layout and page is a separate render unit
architectureImplications: Default component type — opt-in to client behavior, not opt-out
Enforces data-fetching colocation: fetch data in the component that needs it, not a parent
Eliminates the need for API routes to serve data to the frontend — direct DB/service access is idiomatic
Server Component tree and Client Component tree are separate module graphs — a file imported into a Client Component is NOT a Server Component
Enables leaf-node client boundaries: only interactive leaf components need 'use client', keeping most of the tree server-rendered
Third-party components that use client APIs must be wrapped in a Client Component boundary before use in Server Components
Context providers must be Client Components — wrap only the subtree that needs context, not the entire document
server-only package enforces server module boundaries at build time — import it in any file that must never reach the client
performanceImplications: Reduces client-side JavaScript bundle size — Server Component code is never included in JS bundles
Improves First Contentful Paint (FCP) — HTML is generated on server and sent immediately
Enables streaming — slow data fetches can be wrapped in Suspense to unblock fast content
Memoization of identical fetch() calls prevents redundant network requests within a single render
Parallel layout/page rendering — each route segment fetches data concurrently by default
Prerendering (static rendering) at build time eliminates per-request server work for cacheable routes
Fetching data in Server Components avoids client-server waterfalls for initial page loads
commonMisusePatterns: Marking entire layouts or page files as 'use client' — loses all server rendering benefits for that subtree
Using useState or useEffect as a signal to add 'use client' without isolating the interactive part to a leaf component
Fetching data in Client Components when Server Components could fetch it — creates client-server waterfalls
Passing functions or class instances as props from Server to Client Components — causes serialization errors
Using third-party components with client APIs directly in Server Components without wrapping
Wrapping ThemeProvider or other providers around the entire <html> instead of only children — prevents static optimization of outer shell
Not using server-only package in files containing secrets — risks accidental client inclusion
Creating deep prop drilling of server data when React.cache + context pattern would be cleaner
productionRisks: Secret leakage: NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefixed variables are embedded in client bundle — never prefix secrets with NEXT_PUBLIC_
Hydration mismatches: Server-rendered output must match client-rendered output — dynamic values (dates, random IDs) must be consistent
Increased TTFB if Server Components perform slow uncached database queries on every request
Accidental server-only module inclusion in client bundle if server-only package is not used and module is imported transitively by a Client Component
Non-serializable prop errors at runtime if complex objects are passed from Server to Client Components
Cache staleness if revalidation strategy is not configured — stale data served indefinitely after build

valid:
// Parallel data fetching
const [artist, albums] = await Promise.all([getArtist(username), getAlbums(username)])
